title: EMERGENCY PODCAST: DeepSeek shakes the foundation of AI
description: Send us Fan Mail Jimmy and Matt scramble into the AI bunker to sound the alarm with an urgent, emergency episode. In the past week an emerging model from a relatively unknown Chinese developer, DeepSeek, has redefining the entire landscape of AI. At the same time OpenAI, Donald Trump and a bunch of greedy transhumanist were announcing $600bn to build massive brute force compute data centres based on existing LLM architecture. With its open-source approach and a completely new method of inference DeepSeek's models showcase capabilities that challenge the most advanced reasoning models like Open AI's o1 at a fraction of the cost. It has literally sent shockwaves around the AI world. This discussion dives deep into the implications of this shift, exploring the what it means for China and the U.S. in AI development, the potential advancements toward AGI, and the democratisation of AI technology. • DeepSeek emerges as a new open-source model from China • Comparison of DeepSeek's performance with that of US frontier models • Discussion on open-source versus closed-source AI strategies • The implications of DeepSeek's release on geopolitics • The future of AGI and its ethical considerations • Risks of existing companies becoming obsolete without innovation • Potential for increased efficiencies in AI through open-source models • How chip restrictions could have driven innovation in China DeepSeek Is Chinese But Its AI Models Are From Another Planet DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning DeepSeek DeepSeekR1 - Full Breakdown Announcing The Stargate Project | OpenAI This Rumor About GPT-5 Changes Everything
summary: Emergency episode recorded days after DeepSeek R1 detonated the AI world: a roughly $5-6m-trained open-source Chinese reasoning model matching OpenAI's best on math and coding benchmarks at 5-10% of query cost, dropped in the same window as Trump's inauguration and the $500bn Stargate announcement. Jimmy celebrates open source winning and US sanctions forcing Chinese innovation; Matt smells geopolitics and suspects frontier labs already hide better models; both agree brute-force American spending now looks misguided and OpenAI has become too big to fail.
keyTalkingPoints: DeepSeek R1 beats GPT-4-level models on AIME 2024 (79.8% vs 79.2%), MATH-500 (97.3%) and CodeForces (96th percentile); a 7bn-parameter version runs on a laptop and beats GPT-4 at math; queries cost 5-10% of GPT's
Pure reinforcement learning with humans taken out of the loop - genuinely novel methods, fully open-sourced, replicable by anyone

The timing smells: released around Trump's inauguration and Stargate's massive data-center announcement; Matt suspects a geopolitical shot across the bow, or that frontier labs have better models behind closed doors
Stargate is pure brute force versus Chinese efficiency; infrastructure could be obsolete overnight if next year's architectures need different GPUs

AGI under the watered-down 'does things as well as humans' definition is coming pretty soon - but the last 0.01% of capability may be impossible, and Jimmy still sees no genuinely novel ideas, only approximation of training data

OpenAI is now too big to fail - the US government's golden child, like Boeing or Saudi Aramco; enterprise API economics ($1 vs 5 cents per million tokens) is where the money war will be fought, and Operator is Ask Jeeves-style novelty next to the real future: a fine-tuned personal assistant that already knows your preferences

jimmy: DeepSeek proves open source is at or ahead of the frontier and massively democratizes advanced reasoning
US chip sanctions forced Chinese innovation - the West forced China into this direction by denying brute-force compute
Stargate's brute-force spending could be obsolete overnight; the money is going in the wrong direction
matt: The timing and circumstances stink of geopolitics; if it were really this big a breakthrough, would China let it out?
Frontier labs likely already have GPT-5/Opus-3.5-class models behind closed doors, used to train the smaller public releases
AI is something being done to humanity, not something it wants - but the path seems inevitable
